Error.description: The body of any response that is not a 2xx.

Status.description: One failure. `status` names the `google.rpc.Code` and is what a client branches on; `code` is the HTTP status the same failure carries, and `message` is prose that may be reworded in any release.

details.description: Typed detail messages, each tagged with `@type`. `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` carries the stable `reason` a client branches on.

flexiq.v1.CacheConfig.description:
Memoize this node's result and skip re-running it on a later, otherwise
identical, submission.

**`SubmitWorkflow` refuses any graph where a node sets this field**, for the
same reason as GateConfig: nothing reachable from the producer door
resolves a cache hit yet.

job.description:
The job as it stands after the call, carrying neither payload nor result.

A pending job is CANCELLED outright. A running one cannot be stopped from
outside, so it comes back RUNNING with cancel_requested set and the task
stops at its next check. A job already in a terminal state comes back
unchanged, which is what makes calling this twice safe.

flexiq.v1.Debounce.description:
Collapse a burst of enqueues carrying one key into a single run.

While a job with this key is still pending and unclaimed, its scheduled time
slides forward instead of a second job being inserted.

key.description: Non-empty. Jobs sharing it share a window.

maxPending.description:
The producer's own admission cap for the target queue, mirroring the SDK
app config rather than any server-side policy. Absent means uncapped, and
then nothing is counted. Non-negative.

maxWait.description:
Ceiling on the total delay, measured from the pending job's creation.
Mandatory, and at least `window`: without it a producer that never stops
enqueuing starves the job forever.

replacePayload.description:
Overwrite the pending job's payload with this one. False keeps the payload
the window opened with.

window.description: How far ahead of now each enqueue pushes the run. Must be positive.

enqueued.description: Exactly what Enqueue answers, deduplicated included.

error.description: This item alone did not land.

items.description:
The same shape one Enqueue takes, so a client's single-enqueue handling
works unchanged per item.

results.description:
One result per input item, in input order.

**No atomicity is promised**, because not every backend can keep such a
promise. Where a batch is one transaction, an item failure fails the whole
RPC — returning earlier items as enqueued would report jobs that do not
exist — and the error carries the failing item's `index`. Where a batch can
partially apply, the RPC succeeds and an `error` arm means that item alone
did not land. Treating an `enqueued` arm as durable is correct under both.

flexiq.v1.EnqueueOptions.description:
The producer-settable knobs on a job.

Mirrors the producer-settable half of `NewJob` in
crates/flexiq-core/src/job.rs and invents no second vocabulary for the same
values. Two things proto3 cannot express and a client cannot guess:

  * an empty `queue` means "default", substituted server-side;
  * a higher `priority` runs first.

Absent, deliberately: a namespace, which is a property of the credential and
never of a request; and any `idempotent` flag. The `auto:` key is a sha256
over the serialized payload and belongs to the SDKs — a client that wants one
computes it and sends it as `unique_key`.

debounce.description:
Present or absent: the three-of-three validation the SDKs do by hand
becomes a question about the message.

dependsOn.description:
Job ids this job waits on. An id in another namespace is refused exactly as
a missing one is, and reports the same reason.

expiresAt.description: After this instant the job is cancelled instead of dispatched.

maxRetries.description: Attempts after the first. Zero means the job is not retried.

resultTtl.description: How long to keep the result after completion.

uniqueKey.description:
Dedupes against the **active** job carrying the same key, in the caller's
own namespace. It is not an idempotency key without an expiry: a retry
that arrives after the original finished enqueues a second job.

raw.description:
The tagged envelope from BINDING_CONTRACT.md — one tag byte followed by
CBOR [args, kwargs]. Reaches storage untouched.

structured.description:
Arguments the server encodes into that same envelope. Refuses the values
it cannot encode losslessly rather than rounding them, and does not
preserve object key order — see StructuredArgs.

taskName.description: The registered task to run. Not validated here; see the service comment.

deduplicated.description:
The unique_key matched a job that was already active, and this is that job
rather than a new one.

Every other response field describes resulting state rather than what the
call did. This one is the exception, because it is the whole reason a
producer sets a unique_key: without it the two calls are indistinguishable.

flexiq.v1.FanInConfig.description:
Collect a fan-out's expanded results back into one node.

**`SubmitWorkflow` refuses any graph where a node sets this field**, for the
same reason as FanOutConfig.

flexiq.v1.FanOutConfig.description:
Expand this node into one job per item at runtime.

**`SubmitWorkflow` refuses any graph where a node sets this field.** Runtime
expansion is exactly the kind of thing a live SDK tracker does and a
stateless RPC cannot.

itemsFrom.description:
The node whose result supplies the items to expand over. Unset infers the
single predecessor structurally, the same inference a fan-out with no
explicit source already falls back to in every shell.

flexiq.v1.GateConfig.description:
A gate: the node pauses and waits for an external decision before running.

**`SubmitWorkflow` refuses any graph where a node sets this field.** Gate
evaluation is driven by a live SDK tracker process today, and nothing
reachable from the producer door can drive one — see WorkflowNodeConfig.
The field exists so the wire never needs a second, breaking pass to add it
once that changes.

onTimeout.description: What a gate does if its timeout elapses with no decision.

nodes.description: Every node the run has, in no particular order.

flexiq.v1.Job.description:
A job, as a reader sees it.

Mirrors the read model in crates/flexiq-core/src/job.rs. Numbers 1-15 encode
in one byte and are spent on the fields every response carries; the optional
tail starts at 16.

Times are google.protobuf.Timestamp and durations are
google.protobuf.Duration. Storage keeps Unix milliseconds, so sub-millisecond
precision is truncated on the way in.

Fields whose absence differs from their zero carry explicit presence. A
message-typed field has presence inherently in proto3, so `optional` appears
only on the scalars that need it.

cancelRequested.description: A cancel was requested while the job was running; the task polls for it.

completedAt.description: An instant, RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset.

createdAt.description: An instant, RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset.

error.description:
Canonical JSON `{errtype, message, traceback[]}` when whatever produced the
error wrote one, and free prose otherwise. Readers fall back on non-JSON.

expiresAt.description: After this instant the job is cancelled instead of dispatched.

hasDeps.description: The job waits on at least one dependency.

id.description: Opaque. A UUIDv7 today; read it as a string, never as a UUID.

metadata.description:
Opaque JSON text, byte-preserved. Not a Struct: a Struct round trip
reorders keys and cannot hold every value this field already carries.

namespace.description:
Output-only, and always the caller's own. It is here so a client logging a
job record has it, not so a client can select one — no request carries a
namespace.

payload.description:
The tagged envelope from BINDING_CONTRACT.md, opaque and never re-encoded.

Absent means the caller did not ask for it; present and zero-length means
the job carries no body. They are different answers, which is why this is
`optional bytes` and not a bare `bytes`.

result.description:
The task's return value, opaque.

Absent means the job returned nothing — or that the caller did not ask for
it; present and empty means it returned an empty value.

resultTtl.description: How long the result is kept after completion.

scheduledAt.description: When the job becomes eligible to run.

startedAt.description: An instant, RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset.

status.description:
Lifecycle state of a job.

One-to-one with `JobStatus` in crates/flexiq-core/src/job.rs, but offset by
one: the Rust discriminants start at `Pending = 0` and zero is spent here on
`_UNSPECIFIED`. The conversion is an exhaustive match with no wildcard, so
adding a variant on either side fails to compile rather than silently
mapping to something wrong.

A reader that does not recognise a value must treat the job as **not
terminal** — never as failed. Only the values it knows are terminal are.

timeout.description: How long one attempt may run before the scheduler reclaims it.

jobs.description:
Newest first. Rows never carry payload or result — a page of a hundred jobs
would otherwise be a page of a hundred payloads. Read one with GetJob.

nextPageToken.description: Empty when this is the last page.

flexiq.v1.StructuredArgs.description:
A call the server encodes into the payload envelope on the caller's behalf.

The other arm of EnqueueRequest.body, `raw`, carries the envelope from
BINDING_CONTRACT.md verbatim and loses nothing; it is what an SDK sends. This
one exists so a client with no CBOR library — a shell script, `curl`, a
language whose ecosystem has no codec — can still submit a job. The server
encodes these values into that same envelope, so storage never holds two
formats and a worker cannot tell which door a job arrived through.

Two consequences of being JSON-shaped. Both are permanent, and neither is a
footnote:

  1. **Values JSON cannot hold are refused, not rounded.** A number here is a
     double, so an integer is carried only up to a magnitude of 9007199254740991
     (2^53 - 1). 2^53 is refused along with everything past it, because it is
     also what 2^53 + 1 rounds to and no server can tell the two apart.
     Anything beyond the range fails with INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than being
     silently truncated, and a non-finite number is refused outright. Byte strings and CBOR tags have no Value arm at all.
     contracts/wire-vectors.json pins exactly those cases as decode-only
     because no JSON-shaped writer can produce them — `raw` is the door that
     carries them.
  2. **Object key order is not preserved.** A protobuf map is unordered, so
     keys reach the envelope sorted. Nothing decodes differently, a CBOR map
     being unordered too — but the bytes differ from what an SDK would have
     sent for the same call, so an SDK's automatic `auto:` idempotency key,
     which is a hash over those bytes, will not match across the two doors. A
     caller that wants deduplication sets EnqueueOptions.unique_key, which is
     the only mechanism this door has in any case.

kwargs.description:
Keyword arguments. A language with no keyword arguments sends none; the
envelope still carries the empty map, because the call body is always a
two-element array.

flexiq.v1.SubWorkflowSpec.description:
A child workflow, submitted and tracked as part of running this node.

**`SubmitWorkflow` refuses any graph where a node sets this field.**
Recursive on WorkflowGraph rather than a bespoke transport: a child node
already carries its own args on its own `body` oneof, so nothing here needs
a second, parallel payload map the way today's per-SDK sub-workflow
transports each independently invented one.

deferredNodeNames.description:
Node names in `graph` whose job is not pre-enqueued at submission — an
SDK tracker creates it at runtime once its gating condition resolves.

flexiq.v1.SubmitWorkflowRequest.description:
Submit a workflow graph for execution.

Refused, FAILED_PRECONDITION, naming the offending node, if any
WorkflowNodeConfig sets gate, cache, fan_out, fan_in or sub_workflow — see
WorkflowNodeConfig's per-field comments. A graph that clears that check is
pre-enqueued as one Job per node, chained by the graph's edges, exactly as
an equivalent call through an SDK's own submit_workflow would be; any
worker with workflow tracking enabled advances it, whether or not it is the
caller that submitted the graph.

There is no caller-supplied version: every submission is version 1 of
`name`. Resubmitting `name` with a graph that differs from what version 1
already holds is refused, INVALID_ARGUMENT — never silently reused —
because a run's definition must describe the graph that produced its jobs.
Submit a materially different graph under a different `name` until this
gains a real version field.

paramsJson.description:
Arbitrary caller data attached to the run, opaque JSON text and
byte-preserved — the same convention as Job.metadata, not the raw/structured
envelope: it is data the run carries, never a call a task receives.

flexiq.v1.WorkflowGraph.description:
A workflow's shape: which steps exist, how they depend on one another, and
each step's own configuration.

Two independent pieces, matching how a workflow is actually built and
compiled server-side (crates/flexiq-python/src/py_workflow/mod.rs): a bare
graph of node names and edges, and a name-keyed configuration map. Neither
this message nor WorkflowNodeConfig ever carries `dag_data` — the JSON
dagron_core::SerializableGraph produces internally. This message compiles
into that form; it does not transmit it.

nodeConfigs.description:
Every non-empty node in `nodes` must have exactly one entry here, keyed by
WorkflowNodeConfig.name.

flexiq.v1.WorkflowGraphEdge.description: One edge, `from` must complete before `to` becomes eligible.

flexiq.v1.WorkflowGraphNode.description:
One node in the graph's shape. The node's configuration lives in the
matching WorkflowNodeConfig, not here — this message carries only what the
DAG itself needs.

flexiq.v1.WorkflowNode.description: One node's state within a run.

completedAt.description: An instant, RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset.

jobId.description:
Unset while the node has not yet been enqueued (deferred nodes, before an
SDK tracker creates their job).

startedAt.description: An instant, RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset.

status.description:
Status of one node within a run.

One-to-one with `WorkflowNodeStatus` in crates/flexiq-workflows/src/node.rs.
The numbers were the core's discriminants offset by one until READY was
removed in 2.0.0; they are wire values now, so the mapping is the explicit
table in grpc/producer/convert.rs and nothing may be renumbered to restore
the arithmetic.

flexiq.v1.WorkflowNodeConfig.description:
One node's configuration: what it runs, and how it relates to the workflow
around it.

Every StepMetadata field (crates/flexiq-workflows/src/definition.rs:9-45)
has a typed home here, including the five that are opaque JSON strings
server-side today — gate, cache, fan_out, fan_in, sub_workflow — so the wire
never needs a breaking pass to type them later. `args_template` and
`kwargs_template` do not appear: a node's arguments travel on `body`, the
same oneof EnqueueRequest already uses, and `kwargs_template` had no reader
in any shell.

Fields 1-15 fit the one-byte range (see job.proto's Job message) because
every field here is a real per-node decision, not a hot path some caller
skips.

compensate.description:
The task to run if this node needs to be rolled back by a saga
compensation. A task name, never JSON.

condition.description: How an inbound edge gates this node. Unset behaves as ALWAYS.

name.description: Matches a WorkflowGraphNode.name in the same WorkflowGraph.

taskName.description: The registered task to run. Not validated here; see ProducerService.

timeout.description: A span of time, seconds with up to nine fractional digits and a trailing `s`.

flexiq.v1.WorkflowRun.description:
A workflow run, as a reader sees it.

Mirrors crates/flexiq-workflows/src/run.rs. Fields whose absence differs
from their zero carry explicit presence.

completedAt.description: An instant, RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset.

createdAt.description: An instant, RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset.

parentRunId.description:
Set when this run is a sub-workflow: the parent run and the node in it
that started this run.

startedAt.description: An instant, RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset.

state.description:
Lifecycle state of a workflow run.

One-to-one with `WorkflowState` in crates/flexiq-workflows/src/state.rs,
offset by one the same way JobStatus is: zero is spent here on
`_UNSPECIFIED`, and the conversion is an exhaustive match with no wildcard.
A reader that does not recognise a value must treat the run as **not
terminal**.

bearerAuth.description: An API token, minted by `flexiq-server token`. It carries the namespace, so no request names one.

info.description:
The JSON facade of the FlexiQ gRPC producer door, transcoded from `contracts/proto/flexiq/v1`. Every path here reaches the same service method a gRPC client reaches, on the same listener and behind the same token check.

Requests are refused when they carry a field the contract does not declare. Responses are not closed: a later release may add one.

A listener serves exactly one namespace and it comes from the token, so no request names one. A job in another namespace is indistinguishable from a job that does not exist.

This document is generated. Edit `contracts/proto/flexiq/v1/producer_service.proto` and run `scripts/proto-check.sh --fix`.
info.summary: Submit work, read it back, cancel it, count it.

Lifecycle state of a job.

one: the Rust discriminants start at `Pending = 0` and zero is spent here on
`_UNSPECIFIED`. The conversion is an exhaustive match with no wildcard, so
adding a variant on either side fails to compile rather than silently
mapping to something wrong.

A reader that does not recognise a value must treat the job as **not
terminal** — never as failed. Only the values it knows are terminal are.

parameters.description:
Rows per page. Zero takes the server's default; the server may return
fewer, and may cap a large value.
parameters.name: pageSize

parameters.description:
The previous response's next_page_token. Opaque: its contents are free to
change between backends and between releases, so a client passes it back
and interprets nothing.
parameters.name: pageToken
